routes.description: Establish Christian revelation as the necessary precondition for intelligible truth, logic, knowledge, induction, and evidence, then argue that skeptical or naturalistic alternatives cannot supply those preconditions without circularity or borrowing them.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if God and Christian revelation are shown to be necessary for the rational practices used in assessing the motion, while the proposed nonrevelatory foundations fail to account for those practices and rival-revelation objections are resolved.

motionBridge.description: Connect the necessity of the Christian God for intelligibility to the conclusion that belief in God is reasonable under the debate motion.

centralBridges.description: Require divine revelation to ground objective truth, access to reality, and knowledge despite skeptical possibilities.
Account for logical necessity and rational thought as reflections of God's mind rather than unexplained natural processes.
Show that nonrevelatory appeals to past experience cannot non-circularly justify induction or expectations about the future.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Explain why evidence is assessed within a God-grounded framework rather than from a purportedly neutral standpoint.
Distinguish Christian revelation from competing religious claims and internal Christian disagreement sufficiently to support the specifically Christian foundation.

routes.description: Apply an evidential and fallibilist standard of reasonable belief, defend practical truth-seeking through shared experience, logic, and probabilistic induction, and require independent support for God, supernatural causation, revelation, and Christianity's claimed exclusivity.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if reasonable inquiry can proceed without absolute certainty or Christian revelation and if presupposing God does not independently demonstrate divine existence, explanatory necessity, reliable revelation, or warranted belief in the specifically Christian claim.

motionBridge.description: Connect the absence of a valid, sound, and adequately evidenced demonstration of God to withholding belief under the motion's reasonableness standard.

centralBridges.description: Establish that justified belief and practical inquiry do not require infallible access to ultimate reality or a solution to hard solipsism.
Account for truth-seeking, logical reasoning, and induction through reality, shared experience, and evidence-proportioned confidence.
Require demonstration that Christianity uniquely grounds rational intelligibility rather than treating that exclusivity as a premise or shifting its burden.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Test whether conflicting revelations, scriptural claims, and transmission history provide a reliable method for identifying divine disclosure.
Require a demonstrable method or causal connection before supernatural explanations can support reasonable God-belief.

sections.title: Reasonableness, Burden of Proof, and Presuppositional Method
sections.rationale: This issue fixes the motion-level standard and determines whether God may be treated as the prerequisite of adjudication or must be supported through shared argumentative and evidential standards.

sections.title: Truth, Knowledge, Certainty, and Hard Solipsism
sections.rationale: The central epistemic clash concerns whether knowledge requires divinely guaranteed access to ultimate reality or whether fallible, reality-directed inquiry can support reasonable belief without absolute certainty.

sections.title: Logic, Reason, and Worldview Grounding
sections.rationale: This section addresses whether logical absolutes and rational cognition require the Christian God, and whether naming God as their foundation supplies a demonstrated and uniquely necessary account.

sections.title: Induction, Evidence, and Supernatural Inquiry
sections.rationale: The parties dispute whether probabilistic inference from experience is rationally adequate, whether it is problematically circular, and what evidential method could warrant supernatural causation.

sections.title: Revelation, Rival Claims, and Christian Specificity
sections.rationale: Because the affirmative foundation is specifically Christian revelation, the burden structure includes how revelation is identified, how competing religious claims are distinguished, and how internal disagreement bears on reliability.

chunk-001:c001.proposition: Belief in God is reasonable because God exists, while denying God reduces the opposing worldview to absurdity.

chunk-001:c003.proposition: Without divine revelation, a person who cannot escape solipsism or know ultimate reality cannot claim to know anything as true.

chunk-001:c008.proposition: Arguments using truth and logic borrow resources that a godless worldview cannot ground, while biochemical causation alone cannot distinguish sound reasoning from physical output.

chunk-002:c002-06.proposition: Truth conforms to the mind of God, and without that divine standard no person can know anything to be true.

chunk-002:c002-07.proposition: Using sense and reason to establish the past, present, or future reliability of those same faculties is viciously circular and cannot ground knowledge.

chunk-002:c002-08.proposition: All evidence points to God because no evidence is intelligible unless God is accepted as its necessary precondition.

chunk-003:chunk-003-candidate-04.proposition: Attempting to validate future-directed inductive reasoning by appealing to its past success uses induction itself and therefore begs the question.

chunk-003:chunk-003-candidate-07.proposition: Logical absolutes are accounted for as reflections of God's thinking and are known by human beings through divine revelation.

chunk-004:chunk-004-candidate-02.proposition: Islam is internally refuted because the Quran affirms the Bible and denies that God's words can be corrupted, while the Bible contradicts Islam.

chunk-004:chunk-004-candidate-06.proposition: Christian disagreements concern peripheral matters, while the essential revelation teaches creation in God's image, human rebellion, estrangement, and salvation through Jesus.

chunk-001:c005.proposition: Belief in God is unreasonable until the claim is supported by a valid, sound, evidential demonstration, because accepting unsupported claims by default permits contradictory beliefs.

chunk-001:c006.proposition: Conflicting religions and divisions within Christianity offer incompatible purported revelations but no verifiable method for determining which alleged divine disclosure is true.

chunk-001:c007.proposition: God-belief lacks reasonable evidential support when supernatural causation has no testable verification mechanism and produces none of the reliable manifestations that a capable God could provide.

chunk-001:c009.proposition: Although hard solipsism has no known ultimate solution, practical inquiry can proceed from minimal commitments to existence, reason, and generally reliable experience without assuming God.

chunk-001:c010.proposition: Invoking God to ground logical absolutes adds an undemonstrated entity without explaining logical necessity or establishing that the proposed Christian account is uniquely required.

chunk-002:c002-04.proposition: Reality itself, rather than any person's internal representation of it, determines whether competing beliefs are correct, while inquiry improves the accuracy of those representations.

chunk-002:c002-05.proposition: Reasonable belief in God requires valid argument and evidentially supported premises just like other propositions, rather than presupposition, immunity from disproof, or appeal to ignorance.

chunk-003:chunk-003-candidate-03.proposition: Induction rationally supports probabilistic predictions from observed past patterns without claiming certainty that future events must conform to those patterns.

chunk-003:chunk-003-candidate-06.proposition: Claiming that Christianity alone accounts for logical absolutes does not establish that conclusion unless the proposed account and its asserted exclusivity are demonstrated.

chunk-004:chunk-004-candidate-05.proposition: Textual fidelity and incidental historical details do not establish biblical truth; individual biblical claims and any alleged revelatory mechanism require independent demonstration.
